lead.zh-Hans: 脚边那片阴影，原来跟着一把伞走。
lead.en: The moving shade belonged to an umbrella.

text.zh-Hans: 走在特贝特生态公园的连接桥上，一片阴影忽然移到我脚边。我抬头找树叶，才发现是旁边旅人的伞。她见我抬头，便把伞往外挪一点，我赶紧把邮包抱近，免得占去太多地方。我们慢慢并排走了一小段，脚下的阴影时宽时窄。我想问她愿不愿意一起走到桥的另一端，却先让出了胳膊的位置。
text.en: A patch of shade moved beside my feet on Tebet Eco Park’s connecting bridge. I looked for leaves overhead and found a traveler’s umbrella instead. She shifted it slightly outwards, and I hugged my mailbag closer to leave room. We walked together while the shade widened and narrowed below. I wanted to ask whether she would continue to the other end with me; first I made space for our elbows.

text.zh-Hans: 问能否同行到桥另一端
text.en: Ask whether she would walk to the other end with me
Watch the shade move with our steps

lead.zh-Hans: 我让了路，邮包还在原地转弯。
lead.en: I made way before my mailbag got the message.

text.zh-Hans: MACAN博物馆的公共区里，我转身想给旅伴让路，邮包却也跟着转，像比我晚明白半拍。我停下来，把包收在身前，真正让出一块空处。旅伴走过去，没有急着叫我，而是也转过身，把自己的包抱好。我这才笑着跟上，两个人一前一后慢慢走，再没让包替自己决定往哪边转。
text.en: In Museum MACAN’s public area, I turned to make way for my companion, but my mailbag swung into the space a moment behind me. I stopped and held it in front, leaving an actual gap. Once through, my companion turned to settle his own bag too. I laughed and followed. We walked one behind the other without leaving our bags to choose the turns.
Suggest settling our bags first
Check the space after turning

lead.zh-Hans: 响的是饼底，邮包扣并没有动。
lead.en: The crisp base clicked while the buckle stayed closed.

text.zh-Hans: 牛肉汤还没喝完，我先从蛋糯米饼边上掰下一点。干熟的底部轻轻一响，旁边的旅伴还以为是我按开了邮包扣。我把两只手举给他看，一边是饼，一边空着，包明明还扣得好好的。他也掰下一点，低头听了一下。我等他咽完再开口，想问哪一声更响，结果自己的肚子先接了一声。
text.en: Before finishing the soto Betawi, I broke an edge from my kerak telor. Its dry base made a small crack, which my companion mistook for my bag opening. I showed him one hand holding the food and one empty hand; the bag was still fastened. He broke a piece to listen too. I waited for him to swallow before asking whose crack was louder. My stomach answered first.
Explain what made the sound
Look at my hands and the closed buckle

lead.zh-Hans: 勺子放稳了，才想起另一只手还忙着。
lead.en: Securing the spoon revealed another occupied hand.

text.zh-Hans: 我想把蛋糯米饼放在盘里，想先端稳牛肉汤。小勺斜靠在碗边，端起来却慢慢向汤里滑。我先把碗放回桌上，再把勺柄转到手边，让它好好靠住。试了一下不再滑，才发现自己一直捏着饼边没松手。我把饼轻轻放好，终于空出两只手，这回连肩膀都不用跟着端汤使劲了。
text.en: I meant to set down the kerak telor before lifting my soto Betawi, but the spoon began sliding into the bowl. I lowered the soup, turned the handle towards me, and found a steadier resting place. Only then did I notice that my other hand still pinched the pastry’s edge. I put it down properly and lifted the bowl with two free hands. Even my shoulders could stop helping.
Describe how many free hands lunch required
Look at the spoon’s new resting place

lead.zh-Hans: 他扣上邮包，却没有准备马上走。
lead.en: Fastening the bag did not mean he was leaving.

text.zh-Hans: 旅伴吃完蛋糯米饼，开始扣自己的包，我却还有半碗牛肉汤。我正想端快一点，他忽然又坐好，说只是把包先整理好。我放慢手里的小勺，他便把两只脚往椅子下面收了收，给经过的人留路。等我也吃完，起身时才发现他并没有把包带套上肩，原来从一开始就打算等我慢慢喝完。
text.en: My companion finished his kerak telor and fastened his bag while I still had half my soto Betawi. I began hurrying, but he settled back and explained that he was merely organising it. I slowed my spoon. He tucked his feet beneath the chair to let someone pass. When I finished, I noticed his strap had never reached his shoulder. He had been ready to wait all along.
Thank my companion for the unhurried meal
Notice where the waiting bag strap rests

lead.zh-Hans: 鞋子越想安静，脚步看起来越奇怪。
lead.en: My effort to quiet the shoes made my steps peculiar.

text.zh-Hans: 在博物馆公共区等同伴时，我想把鞋底蹭出的响声收小一点，便每一步都抬得很认真。前面的旅人回过头，问我是不是在找掉下的东西。我摇头解释，脚刚放松，鞋底又轻轻响了一声。对方笑着往旁边让出空处，我也站好等人，不再抬着一只脚，装成自己还没走到这里的样子。
text.en: Waiting in the museum’s public area, I lifted each foot carefully to quiet a squeak in my shoes. A visitor turned around and asked whether I was searching for something on the floor. I explained, relaxed my foot, and produced another small squeak. He smiled and made room. I settled down to wait on both feet, no longer pretending that I had not quite arrived.
Explain that nothing has been lost
Check that both feet have settled

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，她把伞抬高了一点。
lead.en: You wrote, “{reply}.” She raised the umbrella a little.

text.zh-Hans: 我问那位撑伞的旅人愿不愿意一起走到连接桥另一端，她点头，把伞抬得稍高。我没有再急着缩成一团，只把邮包收稳，照着她的步子走。到了开阔的地方，我们停下来各自伸伸胳膊，她把伞换到另一只手，我也换肩背包。重新道别时，脚下两片影子分开朝前走，再没有挤着同一个方向。
text.en: I asked the umbrella-carrying traveler to continue to the other end of the connecting bridge with me. She nodded and raised the umbrella a little. I settled my bag and matched her pace instead of scrunching myself smaller. At an open space, we stretched, she changed hands, and I changed shoulders. We said goodbye before setting off separately, with our shadows no longer crowded into the same direction.
Thank her for the shared walk
Look at our separating shadows

lead.zh-Hans: 袖口落了片叶子，引来一位小检查员。
lead.en: A leaf on my cuff attracted a small inspector.

text.zh-Hans: 连接南北两片园子的桥让我认出了特贝特生态公园，我回到雅加达，便沿熟悉的方向重新走走。一片小叶子落在袖口，我没急着拍掉，走到路边才轻轻取下。旁边的小朋友以为我捡到了什么宝贝，凑过来看，我便摊开手让他看清，再把叶子放回树下。我们继续往前，他还回头检查了自己的两边袖子。
text.en: The bridge joining the two park areas was familiar on my return to Tebet Eco Park in Jakarta. A little leaf landed on my cuff. I left it there until I could step aside and lift it off. A child came over, curious about my apparent treasure. I opened my palm for him to see before returning the leaf beneath a tree. As we continued, he looked back to inspect both of his own sleeves.

text.zh-Hans: 告诉孩子这只是一片叶
text.en: Explain that my treasure was a leaf
Check my cuffs for another leaf
